_comment: Declared exceptions to skill_audit.py defaults. Each is a decision, not a threshold tweak — the justification is the point, and it is reviewable in the diff.
_skill_md_budget_why: Default is 3000. The triage protocol (~690 tokens) and the four escalation triggers (~180 tokens) live in the always-loaded tier because they are what prevents naive multi-file loading. They cost ~870 tokens once per conversation and save ~4,000 on a typical two-reference task, and more on tasks that would otherwise pull four files. Raising the budget is the correct trade; trimming them would restore the bloat they exist to prevent. Revisit if SKILL.md exceeds 3700.
_core_sections_why: These are not summaries of a reference — they are always-needed content that belongs in the always-loaded tier. The function and comment procedures apply to every code-writing task, so handing off to functions.md/comments.md for the basic procedure would guarantee a load on every task. They deliberately have no escalation trigger.
_partial_access_why: 5,145 tokens, but it is a lookup table, not prose. SKILL.md Step 3 documents grep-by-ID (~60 tokens per entry) and index-only browse (~630 tokens). Its total size is not what a task actually pays. Splitting it would break the grep-one-file access pattern that makes it cheap.
